newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JUNE 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JUNE 12.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:

--Those with big tax bills owed to the state have been put in the firing line of the tax office's campaign to increase revenues, shortly before a new bill is submitted to Parliament providing for 'realistic fines'. Deputy Finance Minister George Drys said he would use "all means" to recoup the 1.5 trillion drachmas.

--The government is planning a 1.7 trillion drachma investment in energy resources - incuding 150 billion for renewable sources - over the next five years, Development Minister Vasso Papandreou said yesterday.
--Queues to buy OTE shares yesterday bumped up prices a healthy 4.9 percent: domestic interest in the second share offer is particularly intense.

--The national economy ministry is preparing a new bill on subsidies, replacing the present system with two new forms of subsisidisation: tax breaks, and subsisidised interest rates on investment loans.
--Inflation will show its hard core in June, according to sources who say that it is not expected to decrease significantly but may also display a tendency to dig in and maybe even claw back upwards.
--The government will place emphasis on light industry in revisions to the development law, according to reports.

--Developments in the Greek economy will be the focus of a meeting chaired by Prime Minister Costas Simitis today. The meeting is expected to be a review of developments in the European Union, in light of next week's summit.

--The protracted issue of the pricing of medicines will go straight to the prime minister for resolution given that none of the competent ministers are willing to take the responsibility. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
